summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent and the top-priority order is still correct, but the canonical priority surface needed a refresh in this run. Priority 1 remains the dominant bottleneck; however, it has advanced from preparation-only to a bounded approval-and-verification path. New 2026-03-19 artifacts now define approval scope, verification framing, exemplar-backfill requirements, and a draft canonical intake contract for the low-risk path of keeping the existing TDE task model with required improvement metadata, source linkage, and closure-evidence rules. Priority 2 remains unchanged and unstarted, with interim-copy drift still the live distribution mode. Priority 3 remains partially advanced: the first full incident-to-improvement proof case is still closed, and there is now a bounded Phase 1 intake contract, but the broader minimum cross-product improvement interface is not yet fully codified or deployed.
materialChanges: TOP_PRIORITIES.md was updated in this run. The rank order did not change, but Priority 1 and Priority 3 status text were stale relative to the 2026-03-19 execution artifacts.
Priority 1 gained a bounded approval-and-verification chain on 2026-03-19: approval scope, verification frame, exemplar backfill spec, and draft canonical intake contract.

The low-risk substrate path is now stronger than in the prior report: keep the existing canonical TDE task model and enforce required fields for source linkage and closure evidence instead of inventing a separate task class or board.
Priority 3 now has a bounded Phase 1 intake contract for canonical improvement work, but that contract has not yet been promoted into the full minimum product-side interface across active products.
No new execution evidence appeared for pinned-lane delivery into PXS. Interim-copy drift remains unchanged.

topPriorities.title: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record
topPriorities.why: Improvement still lacks a formally approved and enforced canonical substrate in TDE terms. Without that, improvement signals can enter TDE, but they do not yet follow one explicit, reusable, verifiable path.
topPriorities.currentStatus: The bottleneck is unchanged, but the product now has a bounded approval-and-verification path. The 2026-03-19 artifacts support the low-risk route of using the current TDE model plus required improvement metadata, evidence linkage, and closure-evidence rules. Approval and enforcement updates are still missing.
topPriorities.nextStep: Approve the canonical improvement substrate using the current TDE model plus required fields (`source_system`, `source_reference`, `product_scope`, `evidence_links`, `improvement_type`, `expected_closure_evidence`); update the named enforcement surfaces; then backfill and validate OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 as the first compliant exemplar batch.

topPriorities.title: Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics
topPriorities.why: Improvement distribution is still not living through a pinned-lane path with machine-checkable installed-version truth. Interim-copy drift remains the active exposure.
topPriorities.currentStatus: No new delivery evidence. Interim-copy lanes remain the baseline mechanism.
topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.title: Roll out the minimum improvement interface across active products, starting with mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion
topPriorities.why: The product has one verified proof case and now a bounded Phase 1 intake contract, but the broader minimum interface is not yet fully codified or deployed across active products.
topPriorities.currentStatus: IMP-ERR-20260315 remains the completed proof case. OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 remain the next live signal batch. A bounded canonical intake contract now exists, but cross-product interface rollout has not started.
topPriorities.nextStep: Promote the bounded intake contract into the broader minimum product-side improvement interface using IMP-ERR-20260315 and OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069 as reference patterns; then begin deployment across active products.

constraints: Improvement must remain evidence-backed and must not become a narrative-only reporting layer.
Improvement does not own canonical task/decision state; that boundary remains with Task Management.
No authority or security boundary changes should be made as part of improvement rollout without explicit escalation.
